newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator suggests hiring Hong Kong police.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator suggests hiring Hong Kong police.

text.p: A senior U.S. senator suggested on Friday the government consider hiring up to 200 members of the Royal Hong Kong police to help investigate Asian organised crime in the United States.

Sen. Joseph Biden, a Delaware Democrat, introduced a bill that calls for a study of potential benefits and problems of hiring Hong Kong police officers who leave the force after China takes over the British colony at midnight on June 30.

"If the benefits exist, this legislation authorises the addition of up to 200 former (Hong Kong) officers to assist in the investigation of international drug trafficking, alien smuggling, money laundering and organised crime undertaken by the Justice and Treasury departments," he said in a statement.

"Unfortunately, the capacity of U.S. law enforcement to respond to this threat is limited by the fact that we simply do not have enough agents with the language skills, intelligence background and contacts to infiltrate Asian organised crime.

"As officers of the Royal Hong Kong Police leave their force, U.S. law enforcement agencies may be able to bolster our anti-drug, money laundering, alien smuggling and Asian organised crime capabilities with the unique knowledge of the former officers of the Royal Hong Kong Police," Biden said.
